text:
Carolina's best stretch of the night lasted about four minutes. Sebastian Aho scored shorthanded at 2:09 of the second period, Jackson Blake made it 3-0 at 3:28, and Taylor Hall's slap shot at 6:05 restored a three-goal lead after Roman Kantserov had briefly cut it to 3-1. Chicago never got closer than that again until the third period, and by then CAR 5, CHI 2 was nearly settled.

The scoreboard fit the play. CAR out-chanced CHI 3.73 expected goals to 2.65 and attempted 72 shots to 48, which gives the Hurricanes a 67 percent share of simulated replays. The second period was where the gap opened, 1.54 to 0.82. Blake was the common thread, with a goal and an assist and a 1.51 to 0.30 edge in on-ice expected goals in his 15:54. Mike Reilly collected two assists and Jordan Martinook added a goal and an assist, including the backhand that made it 5-1 early in the third.

Chicago's best answer came late. The third period was even at 1.25 to 1.23 in expected goals, and Oliver Moore's goal at 14:14 came on a 49 percent chance. Spencer Knight allowed 1.27 goals more than the 39 shots against him deserved, while Brandon Bussi saved 24 of 26 and finished 0.65 goals ahead of expectation.
